title: Be used to / get used to
note: PULLED FORWARD 2026-09-02 from the parked b2_be_get_used_to (bank was empty - auto-authored and removed 2026-08-29, do NOT refill from auto). be/get used to + -ing = zvyknout si. Three traps: the -ing (*I am used to work here), be vs get (the state you are in vs the change into it), and used to + verb (the a2_used_to past habit) against be used to + -ing. Kept clear of b1_used_to, which is WOULD for past habits. THICKENED 2026-09-04 by the B1 agent loop: 10 -> 28 items. C11 - the used to / be used to contrast is now drilled in Quiz, so it has its own intro card instead of a single Common mistakes row. B4 the unit's own errors (used to working, am used to work, use to) are chips. B11 the contrast items cue both pieces (use / work). A8 contraction twins closed across every accepts list. E9/G4 a Use wrong is only authored where the error is clearly not English; be/get swaps are real English and carry no wrong. A4 - the two the-demanding sentences are English-forced (the left, the heat), queued in DECISIONS.md.

cards.title: Be used to / get used to
cards.title_cz: Be used to / get used to — zvyknout si
points: Czech **zvyknout si** covers both. English keeps the state and the change apart.
**Not** the past-habit *used to* — that one is over. This one is **now**.

rows: you are already comfortable with it
you are becoming comfortable with it

examples.en: She **got used** to the noise quickly.
examples.cz: Rychle si zvykla na ten hluk.

cards.title: used to · be used to
points: **used to** + verb is a past habit — you stopped.
**be used** to + -ing is how it feels to you now.

rows: I **used to** work in a shop.
a past habit — I don't now
I **am used** to working in a shop.
it is normal for me now
I **got used** to working in a shop.

cards.title: Always -ing
points: **to** in *used to* is a preposition, so a verb after it takes **-ing**.

rows: the state — it is normal for me
I **got used** to it last year.

cards.title: Common mistakes
points: After **used to** here, a verb always takes **-ing**.

rows: ~~I am used to get up early.~~
I am used to **getting** up early.
~~She is getting used to speak English.~~
She is getting used to **speaking** English.

blocks.title: Be used to / get used to · B1

items.en: I'm used to working late.
items.cz: Jsem zvyklý pracovat pozdě.
items.gap: I'm used to ____ late. (work)
accepts: I'm used to working late.
I am used to working late.
items.wrong: I am used to work late.
items.explanation: **be used to** takes **-ing**: used to **working**. Not the infinitive.
items.explanation_cz: **be used to** má **-ing**: used to **working**. Ne infinitiv.

items.en: He isn't used to driving on the left.
items.cz: Není zvyklý jezdit vlevo.
items.gap: He isn't used to ____ on the left. (drive)
accepts: He isn't used to driving on the left.
He is not used to driving on the left.
items.wrong: He isn't used to drive on the left.
items.explanation: Still **-ing** after a negative: isn't used to **driving**.
items.explanation_cz: I po záporu zůstává **-ing**: isn't used to **driving**.

items.en: She is used to speaking English at work.
items.cz: Je zvyklá mluvit v práci anglicky.
items.gap: She is used to ____ English at work. (speak)
accepts: She is used to speaking English at work.
She's used to speaking English at work.
items.wrong: She is used to speak English at work.
items.explanation: **speaking** — the -ing form after *is used to*.
items.explanation_cz: **speaking** — tvar s -ing po *is used to*.

items.en: They are used to getting up early.
items.cz: Jsou zvyklí vstávat brzy.
items.gap: They are used to ____ up early. (get)
accepts: They are used to getting up early.
They're used to getting up early.
items.wrong: They are used to get up early.
items.explanation: *get up* after **used to** becomes **getting** up, like any other verb.
items.explanation_cz: *get up* po **used to** je **getting** up, jako každé jiné sloveso.

items.en: We aren't used to paying so much for lunch.
items.cz: Nejsme zvyklí platit tolik za oběd.
items.gap: We aren't used to ____ so much for lunch. (pay)
accepts: We aren't used to paying so much for lunch.
We are not used to paying so much for lunch.
items.wrong: We aren't used to pay so much for lunch.
items.explanation: **paying** — the preposition *to* is followed by the -ing form, never *pay*.
items.explanation_cz: **paying** — po předložce *to* jde tvar s -ing, nikdy *pay*.

items.en: Are you used to working in a new team?
items.cz: Jsi zvyklý pracovat v novém týmu?
items.gap: Are you used to ____ in a new team? (work)
accepts: Are you used to working in a new team?
items.wrong: Are you used to work in a new team?
items.explanation: A question changes nothing after *used to*: still **working**.
items.explanation_cz: Otázka po *used to* nic nemění: pořád **working**.

items.en: My mother is used to cooking for a large group of people.
items.cz: Moje matka je zvyklá vařit pro velkou skupinu lidí.
items.gap: My mother is used to ____ for a large group of people. (cook)
accepts: My mother is used to cooking for a large group of people.
items.wrong: My mother is used to cook for a large group of people.
items.explanation: **cooking** — after *is used to* the verb carries -ing, not the third person -s.
items.explanation_cz: **cooking** — po *is used to* má sloveso -ing, ne koncovku třetí osoby -s.

items.en: Honza isn't used to living in a big city.
items.cz: Honza není zvyklý bydlet ve velkém městě.
items.gap: Honza isn't used to ____ in a big city. (live)
accepts: Honza isn't used to living in a big city.
Honza is not used to living in a big city.
items.wrong: Honza isn't used to live in a big city.
items.explanation: **living** after *isn't used to* — the negative does not take the -ing away.
items.explanation_cz: **living** po *isn't used to* — zápor -ing neruší.

items.en: Are you used to the noise yet?
items.cz: Zvykl sis už na ten hluk?
items.gap: Are you ____ the noise yet? (use)
accepts: Are you used to the noise yet?
items.wrong: Are you use to the noise yet?
items.explanation: **used to** — a noun after it changes nothing, but the **d** is easy to lose: *use to* is not English.
items.explanation_cz: **used to** — podstatné jméno za tím nic nemění, ale **d** se snadno ztratí: *use to* není angličtina.

items.en: I'm not used to cold weather.
items.cz: Nejsem zvyklý na chladné počasí.
items.gap: I'm not used to ____. (cold weather)
accepts: I'm not used to cold weather.
I am not used to cold weather.
items.explanation: *cold weather* is a noun phrase, so nothing changes after **used to**.
items.explanation_cz: *cold weather* je jmenná fráze, takže se po **used to** nic nemění.

items.en: Jana isn't used to English food yet.
items.cz: Jana si ještě nezvykla na anglické jídlo.
items.gap: Jana ____ used to English food yet. (not be)
accepts: Jana isn't used to English food yet.
Jana is not used to English food yet.
items.explanation: **isn't** — *used to* here sits after **be**, so the negative is *isn't used to*, never *doesn't*.
items.explanation_cz: **isn't** — *used to* tu stojí po **be**, takže zápor je *isn't used to*, nikdy *doesn't*.

items.en: She got used to the noise quickly.
items.cz: Rychle si zvykla na ten hluk.
items.gap: She ____ used to the noise quickly. (get)
accepts: She got used to the noise quickly.
items.wrong: She get used to the noise quickly.
items.explanation: **got** used to = the change happened. **was** used to would mean it was already normal for her.
items.explanation_cz: **got** used to = ta změna proběhla. **was** used to by znamenalo, že jí to už normální přišlo.

items.en: I'm getting used to my new job.
items.cz: Zvykám si na novou práci.
items.gap: I'm ____ used to my new job. (get)
accepts: I'm getting used to my new job.
I am getting used to my new job.
items.wrong: I'm get used to my new job.
items.explanation: The change is still happening, so **getting** used to.
items.explanation_cz: Změna pořád probíhá, takže **getting** used to.

items.en: Ondrej is getting used to his new schedule.
items.cz: Ondrej si zvyká na nový rozvrh.
items.gap: Ondrej ____ used to his new schedule. (be / get)
accepts: Ondrej is getting used to his new schedule.
Ondrej's getting used to his new schedule.
items.explanation: **is getting** used to — he is in the middle of the change, not at the end of it.
items.explanation_cz: **is getting** used to — je uprostřed té změny, ne na jejím konci.

items.en: It took me a month to get used to the food.
items.cz: Trvalo mi měsíc zvyknout si na to jídlo.
items.gap: It took me a month to ____ used to the food. (get)
accepts: It took me a month to get used to the food.
items.wrong: It took me a month to getting used to the food.
items.explanation: After the infinitive *to* here you need the plain **get**: *to get used to*.
items.explanation_cz: Po infinitivním *to* tady potřebuješ základní **get**: *to get used to*.

items.en: I can't get used to the heat here.
items.cz: Nemůžu si zvyknout na tady to horko.
items.gap: I can't ____ used to the heat here. (get)
accepts: I can't get used to the heat here.
I cannot get used to the heat here.
items.wrong: I can't getting used to the heat here.
items.explanation: After **can't** you need the plain verb: can't **get** used to.
items.explanation_cz: Po **can't** potřebuješ základní tvar: can't **get** used to.

items.en: We soon got used to living in a small flat.
items.cz: Brzy jsme si zvykli bydlet v malém bytě.
items.gap: We soon got used to ____ in a small flat. (live)
accepts: We soon got used to living in a small flat.
items.wrong: We soon got used to live in a small flat.
items.explanation: **got** used to marks the change, and **living** keeps the -ing.
items.explanation_cz: **got** used to značí změnu a **living** drží -ing.

items.en: You will get used to the new system soon.
items.cz: Brzy si na ten nový systém zvykneš.
items.gap: You will ____ used to the new system soon. (get)
accepts: You will get used to the new system soon.
You'll get used to the new system soon.
items.wrong: You will getting used to the new system soon.
items.explanation: After **will** the verb is plain: will **get** used to, not *will getting*.
items.explanation_cz: Po **will** je sloveso v základním tvaru: will **get** used to, ne *will getting*.

items.en: Did they get used to the early meeting?
items.cz: Zvykli si na tu ranní poradu?
items.gap: Did they ____ used to the early meeting? (get)
accepts: Did they get used to the early meeting?
items.wrong: Did they got used to the early meeting?
items.explanation: *Did* already carries the past, so **get** stays plain: *Did they get used to…*
items.explanation_cz: *Did* už nese minulý čas, takže **get** zůstává základní: *Did they get used to…*

items.en: It is hard to get used to a new city.
items.cz: Je těžké zvyknout si na nové město.
items.gap: It is hard to ____ used to a new city. (get)
accepts: It is hard to get used to a new city.
It's hard to get used to a new city.
items.wrong: It is hard to getting used to a new city.
items.explanation: *hard to* + plain verb: **get** used to. The -ing belongs after the second *to*.
items.explanation_cz: *hard to* + základní tvar: **get** used to. -ing patří až za druhé *to*.

items.en: My father never got used to email.
items.cz: Můj otec si nikdy nezvykl na e-maily.
items.gap: My father never ____ used to email. (get)
accepts: My father never got used to email.
items.explanation: **got** used to — the change never finished, and *never* does not need *did*.
items.explanation_cz: **got** used to — ta změna nikdy neproběhla a *never* tu nepotřebuje *did*.

items.en: After ten years here, I am used to the noise.
items.cz: Po deseti letech tady jsem na ten hluk zvyklý.
items.gap: After ten years here, I ____ the noise.
accepts: After ten years here, I'm used to the noise.
After ten years here, I am used to the noise.
items.explanation: **am used to** — ten years, so it is normal by now. *Am getting used to* would say the change is still happening.
items.explanation_cz: **am used to** — deset let, takže je to už normální. *Am getting used to* by řeklo, že změna pořád probíhá.

items.en: It's my first week here, so I am getting used to the noise.
items.cz: Je to tady můj první týden, takže si na ten hluk zvykám.
items.gap: It's my first week here, so I ____ the noise.
accepts: It's my first week here, so I'm getting used to the noise.
It's my first week here, so I am getting used to the noise.
It is my first week here, so I'm getting used to the noise.
It is my first week here, so I am getting used to the noise.
items.explanation: **am getting used to** — the first week, so the change is under way. *Am used to* would say it is already normal.
items.explanation_cz: **am getting used to** — první týden, takže změna právě probíhá. *Am used to* by řeklo, že je to už normální.

items.en: I used to work in a shop.
items.cz: Dřív jsem pracoval v obchodě.
items.gap: I ____ in a shop. (use / work)
accepts: I used to work in a shop.
I am used to working in a shop.
I'm used to working in a shop.
items.wrong: I used to working in a shop.
items.explanation: **used to work** is the past habit — plain verb, no *be*. *Am used to working* would mean it feels normal now.
items.explanation_cz: **used to work** je minulý zvyk — základní tvar, bez *be*. *Am used to working* by znamenalo, že mi to teď připadá normální.

items.en: Now I am used to working in a shop.
items.cz: Teď už jsem zvyklý pracovat v obchodě.
items.gap: Now I ____ in a shop. (be used / work)
accepts: Now I am used to working in a shop.
Now I'm used to working in a shop.
items.wrong: Now I am used to work in a shop.
items.explanation: **am used to working** — the state you are in now. *Used to work* would put it in the past.
items.explanation_cz: **am used to working** — stav, ve kterém jsi teď. *Used to work* by to posunulo do minulosti.

items.en: Patrik used to drive to work every day.
items.cz: Patrik dřív jezdil do práce autem každý den.
items.gap: Patrik ____ to work every day. (use / drive)
accepts: Patrik used to drive to work every day.
items.wrong: Patrik used to driving to work every day.
items.explanation: **used to drive** — a habit he has stopped. There is no *be*, so there is no -ing.
items.explanation_cz: **used to drive** — zvyk, kterého nechal. Není tu *be*, takže není ani -ing.

items.en: He is used to driving in heavy traffic.
items.cz: Je zvyklý řídit v hustém provozu.
items.gap: He ____ in heavy traffic. (be used / drive)
accepts: He is used to driving in heavy traffic.
He's used to driving in heavy traffic.
items.wrong: He is used to drive in heavy traffic.
items.explanation: **is used to driving** — heavy traffic is normal for him now, so *be* plus -ing.
items.explanation_cz: **is used to driving** — hustý provoz je pro něj teď normální, takže *be* plus -ing.

items.en: Are you getting used to your new keyboard?
items.cz: Zvykáš si na novou klávesnici?
items.gap: ____ you getting used to your new keyboard? (be)
accepts: Are you getting used to your new keyboard?
items.explanation: *getting used to* needs **are**, not *do* — it is the continuous of *be*.
items.explanation_cz: *getting used to* potřebuje **are**, ne *do* — je to průběhový tvar slovesa *be*.

items.en: We weren't used to the heat in summer.
items.cz: Nebyli jsme zvyklí na to horko v létě.
items.gap: We ____ used to the heat in summer. (not be)
accepts: We weren't used to the heat in summer.
We were not used to the heat in summer.
items.explanation: *be used to* takes a form of **be**, so the past negative is **weren't**, never *didn't*.
items.explanation_cz: *be used to* má tvar slovesa **be**, takže minulý zápor je **weren't**, nikdy *didn't*.

items.en: I will never get used to getting up at five.
items.cz: Nikdy si nezvyknu na vstávání v pět.
items.gap: I will never ____ up at five. (get used / get)
accepts: I will never get used to getting up at five.
I'll never get used to getting up at five.
items.wrong: I will never get used to get up at five.
items.explanation: Both *get*s in one sentence: plain **get** after *will*, then **getting** after the preposition *to*.
items.explanation_cz: Dvakrát *get* v jedné větě: základní **get** po *will* a pak **getting** po předložce *to*.
